subject: Re: Post-demo: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler eval — next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.g@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.k@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler eval — next steps

Samir — great to meet earlier, thanks again for carving out the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps based on today's demo and the tradeoffs you called out.

Recap (high level)
- Primary goals: low 99th-percentile tail latency for user-facing inference, predictable unit cost at scale, and capacity guarantees for peak traffic windows.
- Hyperscaler offering pros: broad global availability, familiar tooling. Cons you highlighted: preemptible instances during spot/burst, higher tail-latency variability, and limited control over kernel selection/quantization options.
- Redwood Dedicated pros: reserved non-preemptible pools, deterministic throughput, KV/prefix caching, and ability to pin model versions or fall back to cheaper quantized variants.

Proposed POC (what we recommend you run next)
1) Scope: 2-week Dedicated POC (reserved pool of 4 GPUs mapped to H100-equivalent), run your representative workload (batch and low-latency single-shot).
2) Tests: steady-state throughput, tail latency (95/99/999), cold-start behavior, model-variant quality checks, and failure/fallback scenarios.
3) Deliverables: side-by-side latency/cost report, SLA & capacity matrix, and recommended production config (batching/quantization).
4) Proposed window: Dec 6 — Dec 20. We can shift if you need earlier.

Open questions for you
- Confirm acceptance of 4 GPU reserved pool for the POC (can scale up if needed).
- Do you have any blocking compliance/data-residency requirements beyond what we discussed?
- Who from procurement/security should we loop for matching contracts and SOC2 evidence?

Attachments: eval_plan.xlsx (POC plan & test matrix)

Next step
If that all sounds good I'll: 1) spin up the Dedicated POC config with reserved capacity, 2) share benchmark scripts and a DocuSign MSA/POC addendum, and 3) schedule a kickoff with your engineering team.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus — this looks good. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock dates: 
- Capacity guarantees: when you say "reserved" — is that strictly non-preemptible? If we commit, will those GPUs be isolated to our org or shared?
- Hardware mapping: can you confirm whether the H100-equivalent is virtualized on the hyperscaler or native hardware in Redwood Dedicated? We need to map perf to our current A100 fleet.
- Pricing: can you give an estimated POC cost and an order-of-magnitude yearly committed price for a 4-GPU reserved pool?
- Compliance/data residency: our security lead (Tom Security, tom.security@acme.com) will want SOC2 + data residency guarantees (we are fine with US-only region).

I'm looping procurement (Jennifer) on this thread so we can get a PO template and contract timeline if we move forward. If you can send the benchmark scripts + an SLA matrix we can triage internally this week.

Thanks,
Samir Gupta

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler eval — next steps

Samir / Jennifer / Tom — thanks for the quick responses. Answers inline below and next actions.

Capacity guarantees
- Reserved Dedicated pools are non-preemptible and isolated to your org for the duration of the reservation. You get guaranteed vCPU/GPU slot capacity per the reserved commit. Burst capacity is available as a paid add-on but never steals capacity from reserved pools.

Hardware mapping
- Redwood Dedicated offers physical hosts in our colos mapped to H100-equivalent SKUs (we can share exact accelerator model per region). For fair comparison vs your A100 fleet, we will run the exact same model artifacts under both environments and report normalized throughput and latency.

Pricing (ballpark)
- 2-week POC (4 reserved GPUs): ~$12k — covers reserved capacity + data transfer and dedicated support during the test window.
- Yearly committed 4-GPU reserved pool: ~$90k — includes 24/7 ops, a 99.9% uptime SLA, and priority capacity scaling. I'll follow up with an itemized quote.

SLA & compliance
- Attached: sla_matrix.pdf (outlines uptime targets, incident response, and capacity failover options). We are SOC2 Type II and can provide the cert and an evidence bundle for procurement.

Benchmarking
- Attached: benchmark_instructions.md with scripts and recommended payloads. Steps: run the provided client against both environments for 30 minutes steady-state + 1 hour with synthetic burst pattern. We will coordinate log collection and KV cache warmup periods.

Next actions
1) I'll send a formal POC quote and DocuSign link for the POC addendum (link below).
2) Laura will coordinate onboarding/kickoff and set up the Dedicated pool in the US region.
3) Rachel (CS) will own the test instrumentation and result delivery.

Related links:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACME-2026-007
- DocuSign (POC addendum): https://www.docusign.com/12345/ACME-MSA

Attachments: sla_matrix.pdf, benchmark_instructions.md

If that all looks good I will prepare the quote and a short checklist for your security team. Proposed kickoff: Dec 6.
